purpose: small held-out lexical and prompt transfer check for the Qwen2.5-Omni-3B audio information-flow pilot
selection: literal prespecified list; no random draw, model response, or ASR result used to choose items

render.word_slot_padding: right-pad each word to the longer processed word fragment in its pair/engine; do not trim or normalize
render.outside_slot_requirement: within every engine/pair/phrasing, integer PCM samples before and after the word slot must be exactly equal

system_prompt: Answer the spoken question with the one word the speaker gave. Do not add anything else.

phrasings.suffix: Tell me the word I chose.

evaluation.primary_site: Thinker decoder block post-output at word-slot audio-placeholder positions on prefill only
evaluation.primary_contrast: paired donor-answer flip rate at post-block layer 30 minus layer 31, across all 16 directional cases; report every case
evaluation.primary_endpoint: entire generated answer after stripping leading/trailing whitespace and one terminal punctuation mark equals donor word case-insensitively, with normal EOS; otherwise failure
evaluation.clean_gate: record all clean complete answers; report both intention-to-test denominator 16 and subset where both clean members answer their own words with EOS; never silently drop failures
secondary: donor-oriented first-token logit margin when candidate answer surfaces are single token
full answer including malformed and no-EOS rates
layer-by-layer edit norm and hook count
controls: equal-width wrong-time rows with donor-minus-recipient norm recorded
equal-norm random direction at word rows with seeds 0, 1, 2
terminal-position donor patch at layers 31 and 35 as positive routing control
verify cached vs uncached prefill activation equality
evaluation.interpretation_limit: A repeat of the 30-to-31 answer cliff is a small lexical/wording/voice transfer check, not a general circuit, exact first-use layer, or security finding. Post-block audio rows mix context; late logit shifts can remain even without full answer flips.
